preflight.why: These are heuristic planning aids, not Google quality scores or proof of a defect. Confirm suggested changes with fresh evidence, installed capabilities, search-intent and subject-matter review.

pending_queue.what: Draft content and queued changes are reviewed by an administrator. Some tools write organizational metadata, research records or local files immediately; inspect each tool contract.

gsc_warehouse.what: Local SQLite archive of retrieved GSC observations. Local retention avoids server pruning, but upstream sampling, API limits and missing dates still constrain coverage.

outcome_engine.what: Compare observed clicks and leads around applied edits with a site comparison. Results are observational; confounding and overlapping interventions can remain.

revert_loop.what: Queue a snapshot-restore of a regressed edit as a normal pending change.

lead_events.what: Daily Elementor Pro form-submission counts per page — the money metric; auto-folded into outcome_report.

attention_system.what: Pages are eye-paths, not section stacks: archetype spec BEFORE composing, predicted-heatmap audit AFTER (flat_hierarchy = generic-page smell).

widget_schema.what: Live Elementor control registry — NEVER guess setting keys (typos are silent no-ops); queue validates with did-you-mean. v0.80: containers/sections/columns included; every Elementor write is validated on EFFECTIVE values (new > stored > default) with inert_setting / global_token_overrides_literal / defaults_in_effect warnings; widget_schema(post_id, widget_id) shows stored vs effective vs applies for one element. An absent key is a DEFAULT, not unset.

operator_kit.what: Site stores design skills + bootstrap bundle; a fresh machine rebuilds the whole environment from the site.

operator_brain.what: The site stores the WHOLE operator brain (every memory file + index, every skill, CLAUDE.md, secrets-stripped .mcp.json template) AND the bridge bin/ files. whoami on every site tells every laptop whether it is behind (operator_brain.status) and whether its bridge matches (operator_brain.bridge.status), and pushes relevant_rules (HARD/STRICT + site-specific memories) into the first call. A second laptop must never again open a chat with missing tools or unknown rules: pull, restart, continue.
operator_brain.tools: operator_brain_status, operator_brain_push, operator_brain_pull; CLI bin/brain-sync.php (status|push|pull|bootstrap across every site in .mcp.json)

builders.what: Native Elementor composition (recipes, containers, service pages, spec builds) + Divi surgical module edits, including removing a leftover module from a Theme Builder layout without opening the builder (v0.70).

audit_family.what: Rendered evidence plus local design, accessibility and SEO heuristics. Use current observations; scores do not establish ranking effects or a need to rewrite.

seo_playbook.what: Current source-linked SEO policy served from the shared agent contract. Industry detection does not override evidence or operator constraints.

clarity_heatmaps.what: Optional recorded behavior can help evaluate layout hypotheses. Predicted-attention scores are not measured visitor attention.

session_gate.what: Queued changes require current identity, target and environment evidence. Read rendered evidence for published pages, full editor content for drafts and capability evidence for settings. Metadata-only tools declare their own side effects.

version_drift.what: whoami warns when this site runs an older plugin than the local build, and (v0.79) when the LOCAL bridge is older than the site — the "functions are missing" case — with the exact pull to run.

commodity_router.what: Low-CTR diagnostic candidates with unknown cause. No automatic content-investment, retirement or AI attribution follows from a threshold.

aeo_tracking.what: Dated low-CTR, crawler-request and appearance observations. Crawls do not prove citations; low CTR and search appearances do not confirm AI Overviews.

rank_math_schema.what: Edit Rank Math Schema Builder rows in place by dot path (offers.price etc). The ONLY path to those capitalised postmeta arrays — draft_update_postmeta lowercases the key and flattens the array. %variable% placeholders survive.

stack_introspection.what: Read installed plugins, captured admin menus and redacted settings. Inspect runtime schemas and registered adapter controls before a feature plan; discovery is explicitly incomplete where no adapter is available.

asset_references.what: Find and swap a media URL WHEREVER it is stored — post_content of any post type, postmeta, options, termmeta — searching every spelling (JSON-escaped, protocol-relative, root-relative, http twin). This is the way into plugins that keep content outside post_content and have no dedicated tool: popup overlays, sliders, theme option backgrounds. Serialized values are unserialized/rewritten/re-serialized so length prefixes stay valid; rows holding non-stdClass objects are refused, not risked. media_audit finds the heavy files worth swapping.

render_health_guard.what: Does the page still WORK after a change? Queue captures a rendered-page baseline (empty-state strings, markup-anchored element counts, shortcode leakage, PHP errors, HTTP status); the post-apply audit re-fetches cache-busted and compares. A builder empty-state appearing or an element population vanishing is flagged CRITICAL on the pending row + activity log + dashboard within ~30s of apply. Reports only; never auto-reverts. Companion lint change: failures are split into introduced-by-this-change vs pre_existing-in-current-body, and pre-existing structural failures no longer hard-block unrelated edits.
render_health_guard.tools: (automatic on queue + apply; see lint introduced/pre_existing in queue responses)

setting_writes.what: Read current plugin capability/schema evidence, preview a typed scalar setting change, then use the existing review flow. Unsupported values or inactive controls remain explicit; a stored value does not verify its visible effect.

bulk_term_tagging.what: Assign ONE taxonomy term to MANY posts in a single approval. Solves the two ways wp-admin gets this wrong: its category filter misses products sitting in deeper sub-terms, and its product search matches DESCRIPTIONS so accessories that merely mention a brand get tagged. Matching is title_contains (SQL LIKE on post_title only), in_term (a term AND all its children), or explicit post_ids. Returns a plan with matched / already-tagged / will-change counts before anything is queued; rollback restores the exact prior terms on every post, including posts that had none. Products are eligible here even though they are off-limits to body edits, because term relationships cannot corrupt product content or pricing.

content_strategy.what: Claude discovers and maintains niche scope from existing sources and notes. New content does not need an existing GSC gap.

content_workflow.what: Prepare a source-backed workflow, execute it with the connected agent, then verify actual result IDs. A saved plan is not proof of created or applied content.

content_research.what: Bounded competitor observations and claim candidates with extraction limits; no factual or global-originality certification.

workflows.gsc_analysis: gsc_warehouse_sync -> gsc_warehouse_query (SQL aggregates, never raw dumps) -> outcome_report for applied-edit verdicts.
workflows.page_build: attention_spec(post_id) -> widget_schema for any unverified setting -> compose -> attention_audit + render_probe + page_robustness_audit -> queue.
workflows.page_optimize: verified_page_audit -> content_decision and relevant measurements -> actual editor/capability reads -> concrete draft changes -> review -> fresh rendered verification -> observational outcome review.
workflows.weekly_harvest: Review measured changes and niche opportunities; diagnose each candidate before proposing specific changes. Missing clicks alone do not justify removal.
workflows.bad_outcome: outcome_report -> inspect concurrent changes, measurement coverage and current rendered output -> choose a supported correction or reviewed revert; an observational decline alone does not establish cause.
workflows.new_machine: Fresh laptop: fetch bin/ from GET /operator-kit/bridge -> php bin/brain-sync.php bootstrap --url --user --pass (pulls memory + skills + CLAUDE.md, writes .mcp.json) -> whoami must show operator_brain.status=in_sync and bridge.status=in_sync -> gsc_warehouse_sync. Existing laptop that whoami calls behind: operator_brain_pull (memory/skills) or operator_brain_pull(what=bridge) + MCP restart. After editing memory/skills anywhere: php bin/brain-sync.php push.
workflows.fix_schema: render_probe (who emits what) -> get_rank_math_schema(post_id) for exact dot paths -> draft_update_rank_math_schema -> approve -> render_probe AFTER. Never add a second emitter for a field Rank Math already owns.
workflows.edit_the_unreachable: Discover the actual storage and installed capability. Use supported targeted tools and preview changes. Unavailable control evidence is a specific limitation, not permission to invent a key or UI path.
workflows.image_weight: media_audit (heaviest on disk + which uploads WordPress re-encoded LARGER than the original) -> find_asset_references on the worst offenders to see which pages load them -> replace_asset_reference with a properly sized file. Resize to at most big_image_size_threshold BEFORE uploading; WordPress leaves those files untouched.
workflows.bulk_product_tagging: Hundreds of products need a brand/term? Do NOT hand-click wp-admin. list_product_categories or the taxonomy REST route to confirm the term EXISTS (this tool never creates terms) -> draft_bulk_assign_term(dry_run=true) to see matched/already/will-change -> check the sample titles are the right slice -> queue -> approve. Re-run per brand; 600 targets max per plan.
workflows.find_a_setting: list_installed_plugins -> get_plugin_settings -> inspect_plugin_capability for the exact option/path or element -> draft_update_plugin_setting or the specific supported editor tool -> review -> verify the intended effect.
workflows.new_blog: content_workflow -> inspect scope and existing knowledge -> research and compare reader tasks -> draft_create_post(workflow_id=...) -> verify_content_workflow -> operator reviews the actual draft.

capabilities.hint: This capability index and current tool descriptions share one versioned contract. Observations outrank stale interpretations; preserve explicit operator constraints and re-read changed evidence.
evidence_rules: Report observed facts, editorial interpretations and unknowns separately; cite the exact source and its scope.
Blocked fetches, partial extraction, missing data and an empty parser result cannot prove rendered absence.
Similarity identifies candidates. It does not establish duplication, a shared reader task or SEO harm.
Low CTR does not prove AI impact; crawler requests do not prove citations; before/after associations do not prove causation.
Discover current installed controls, accepted values and dependencies before planning setting changes.
Verify actual WordPress record IDs and source freshness before reporting completed work.

content_strategy_policy.background_execution: A connected Claude session executes the workflow. This feature does not launch an unattended AI runner.
content_strategy_policy.gsc_role: Observed visibility for this property and period, not total market demand or the boundary of the niche.
content_strategy_policy.no_data_meaning: Demand is unmeasured. It does not mean no opportunity.
decision_rules: Similarity discovers candidates; it does not establish duplication or SEO harm.
Create when a distinct reader task and supported niche relationship justify it; no impression minimum is required.
Keep or link complementary pages. Review preservation before merging substitutable pages.
Diagnose technical, demand and measurement changes before prescribing a rewrite.
Research and formatting cannot certify global novelty, expertise or ranking gains.
Persist evidence and alternatives. Do not change a decision without a changed basis.
content_strategy_policy.result_verification: Link new drafts with workflow_id and call verify_content_workflow. Only actual records and current source observations support completion claims; a plan or generated text alone does not.
content_strategy_policy.setting_workflow: Read get_plugin_settings and inspect_plugin_capability. Valid input types do not certify an active feature or rendered effect; use current runtime controls and verify the outcome.

top_rules: For a complete new blog request, use content_workflow and execute its steps. Claude discovers and maintains strategy with discover_content_scope/manage_content_scope; no manual strategy form is required. Use plan_blog_content for topic proposals. Explore supported services, reader questions and useful explanations even with no GSC gaps or rows.
State the niche source, audience, reader task and supported contribution. Missing impressions means unmeasured demand, not no opportunity.
Inspect related stored and rendered content before claiming a gap. Similarity alone cannot certify duplication or absence.
Use a length and format that solve the reader task; no preferred Google word count or fixed quota of facts, quotes or headings.
Use content_decision before refresh or consolidation proposals. Preserve evidence IDs, alternatives, reader goals and the reason for changing an earlier assessment.
Related pages can serve distinct tasks. Keep/link or differentiate when useful; cluster size, low clicks and shared queries do not establish harmful cannibalization.
Diagnose technical state, measurement, query mix, demand and seasonality before prescribing a rewrite. Do not remove useful material because a local score is low.
A permanent merge needs a relevant destination and preservation of unique facts, useful sections, links and language relationships. Missing analytics is not proof of no value.
Use content_research to capture explicit comparable URLs and current own content. Record scope, fetch date and limitations. A blocked page is unknown.
Statistics, tables, quotation markup and authority links are surface observations, not verified first-party research or expertise.
Check primary-source support, attribution, practical usefulness and originality within the inspected sample. Do not invent evidence or claim global uniqueness.
No special AI markup, forced chunk size or citation quota guarantees Google visibility. Experimental GEO results do not establish organic ranking effects.
Preserve native GSC dimensions and raw counts. Query/page totals and page/appearance segments are separate datasets; do not allocate one into the other.
Check measurement version and re-synced dates. Unlisted historical dates may retain legacy inferred data until re-fetched.
Non-Web search appearances and low CTR do not establish AI Overviews or AI-caused click loss. A before/after change is an association unless stronger evidence supports causation.
Use current target-bound evidence and actual editor/plugin schemas before proposing settings or content changes. Parser absence is not proof of rendered absence.
Use descriptive contextual links where they help the next reader task. No ideal link count or mandatory repeated pillar placement applies.
Preserve coherent headings, accessible controls, supported facts, appropriate schema and language relationships. Assess actual defects rather than blindly follow a score.
Apply through the existing reviewed workflow, verify saved and served output, and distinguish completed writes from uncertain cache or transport states.
Inspect plugin capability evidence before setting changes and verify actual workflow results before claiming completion.

evidence_policy.unknown: Missing evidence, CAPTCHA and unsupported controls block proposals. Stored values do not prove visible effects or Google indexing.

result.version_drift: Site runs cc-assistant v0.87.0 but the local build is v0.89.0 — deploy the latest zip; tools added after v0.87.0 will 404 on this site until then.

hard_rules.name: feedback-build-from-scratch-never-duplicate
hard_rules.description: HARD RULE — never duplicate/clone a page (build_service_page or copy). Every page is built from scratch with its own analyzed section set, intent, and 2026-standard check. Cloning leaves source-condition residue.

hard_rules.name: feedback-dom-is-ground-truth-not-parsers
hard_rules.description: HARD RULE: never assert that a link/heading/element is MISSING from a page based on a plugin parser; the rendered DOM is the only ground truth. Parsers have blind spots and one produced a confident false gap that was acted on.

hard_rules.name: feedback-verify-service-exists-before-service-page
hard_rules.description: HARD RULE — never recommend or build a service page for a service the clinic doesn't actually sell. Verify via service_inventory + Aesthetic-style service-card inventory on the relevant pillar BEFORE proposing anything

hard_rules.name: feedback_never_claim_server_slow_without_control
hard_rules.description: HARD RULE - never diagnose caching or server speed from an option value, a HEAD request, or a raw TTFB; each needs a specific control first

hard_rules.name: feedback_never_noindex_pages
hard_rules.description: HARD operator rule 2026-09-06: NEVER propose or queue noindex on any page, any site. A page near position 10 cannot earn clicks yet; noindex removes the chance. Zero-click pages are improved or merged. Plugin dead_inventory advice text was reworded to match.

hard_rules.name: feedback_never_pass_dollar_strings_through_shell
hard_rules.description: HARD - a title or any text with \"$\" must never travel through a bash/PowerShell command line; the shell ate \"$1\" from \"$10,000\" twice (penny-cost 2026-09-05, car-loan-interest 2026-09-06) and the owner caught the mangled cold open on the first second of the video

hard_rules.name: feedback_no_guessing_epistemic_discipline
hard_rules.description: STRICT user prohibition on guessing — label every claim verified/measured/inferred; inference never drives live-site action untested

hard_rules.name: feedback_probe_discipline_positive_controls
hard_rules.description: HARD rule: my own probes are the #1 source of wrong findings — absence claims need a positive control, API names need a source grep, causes need change-and-remeasure

site_rules.name: Always build the plugin zip yourself
site_rules.description: When the plugin needs deploying to a remote site, build the zip without asking. Use the Python zipfile recipe; don't offer "should I zip" — just do it.

site_rules.name: Custom Permalinks plugin overrides slug-based URLs (silent desync)
site_rules.description: WordPress sites with the "Custom Permalinks" plugin active store a custom_permalink postmeta that overrides get_permalink() — slug changes via wp_update_post() do NOT auto-update it, leaving the stale custom URL in place forever

site_rules.name: Draft English version first, queue/approve it, then draft Spanish
site_rules.description: On bilingual sites, draft and queue the EN post first so the reviewer can see what each pending is about; only draft the ES counterpart after the EN is settled

site_rules.name: Geo-anchor priority — White Rock first, East Dallas second, generic Dallas almost never
site_rules.description: For erofwhiterock.com — own "near White Rock Lake" + neighborhood names. Use "East Dallas" when broader reach helps. Reserve generic "Dallas" for NAP/schema and rare referral context. Avoid keyword-stuffed "in Dallas" patterns that compete with hospital systems.

site_rules.name: New blog posts must always include category assignment
site_rules.description: When creating a new post via cc-assistant, always pass category_ids; otherwise the post lands uncategorized and disrupts taxonomy alignment

site_rules.name: WP "Delete" on a duplicate plugin folder triggers uninstall.php for the SHARED plugin slug — wipes ALL data
site_rules.description: WordPress runs uninstall.php whenever the user clicks "Delete" in the Plugins list, REGARDLESS of whether another folder of the same plugin is still active. uninstall.php drops tables by table name (wp_cc_pending_changes, etc.) which is shared across all copies — so deleting one duplicate wipes data for the active copy too.

site_rules.name: WordPress plugin zips on Windows must use forward slashes — never PowerShell Compress-Archive
site_rules.description: PowerShell's Compress-Archive AND .NET System.IO.Compression.ZipFile.CreateFromDirectory write backslash path separators on Windows, which violates the ZIP spec and breaks WordPress plugin uploads (creates new install folder per upload instead of overwriting). Use Python's zipfile module instead.

site_rules.name: avg-position-expansion-artifact
site_rules.description: GSC site-wide avg position drops dramatically when a site publishes a batch of new pages, because the new URLs pull long-tail impressions at positions 50-90+ before they rank. Always frame avg position drops in expansion context before treating as damage.

site_rules.name: cc-assistant Elementor parser must walk widget-internal headings
site_rules.description: icon-box, image-box, accordion, nested-accordion, and posts widgets render H3 tags but the parser only counted heading widgets — caused false 0-H3 flags

site_rules.name: cc-assistant suspicious_chars lint false-positive on Spanish meta
site_rules.description: Plugin's suspicious_chars lint soft-fails Spanish accented chars (á é í ó ú ñ) — misclassifies valid Latin-1 as suspicious. Items still queue.

site_rules.name: cc-assistant-close-loop-v058
site_rules.description: v0.58.0 SHIPPED — propose_revert (snapshot_restore change type), lead-event logging + leads in outcome_report, whoami version-drift warning

site_rules.name: cc-assistant-v0-18-1-fix-for-race-safety-false-positive-on-sibling-pendings
site_rules.description: previous false positive where pre-apply guard refused sibling pendings within a single bulk batch; fixed in v0.18.1 by stamping _cc_assistant_last_internal_apply postmeta and comparing against max(queued_at, that)

site_rules.name: cc-assistant-v0-28-industry-playbook
site_rules.description: cc-assistant v0.28.0 made the SEO playbook industry-aware. Universal core + per-industry overlay composed at runtime, driven by CC_Assistant_Industry_Profile (auto-detect from schema + Yoast/Rank Math local-SEO type + WooCommerce + title keyword corpus; operator override in Settings → General → Industry).

site_rules.name: cc-assistant-v0601-audit-hardening
site_rules.description: v0.60.1 SHIPPED — full adversarial+security audit of v0.54-0.60 (2 agents), 22 findings ALL fixed; TLS verify default ON, uninstall guarded, propose_revert actually works now

site_rules.name: content-drafting-and-optimization-rules
site_rules.description: Four universal rules for every new post/page AND every optimization of an existing post/page: keyword-optimized (GSC + own knowledge), competitor-beat (gap fill), user-first, and unique-insight-data-with-expert-opinions allowed.

site_rules.name: curl-before-schema-edit
site_rules.description: Before recommending ANY schema / JSON-LD edit, curl the live page and read what's actually there. Never hand the operator a 'replace placeholder X' template — you have full live-site access via the plugin + WebFetch/Bash. Use it.

site_rules.name: curl-test-url-before-editing
site_rules.description: BEFORE queueing ANY edit on a WordPress post, curl-test the post's URL to verify (a) it returns 200 (not 301 redirect, not 404), (b) the rendered content actually matches the post being edited, AND (c) any internal links you're about to write actually resolve. Skipping this check stranded 12 widget edits on a redirected page in one session.

site_rules.name: custom-permalinks-pagination-4site-diagnostic
site_rules.description: When pagination breaks on one bilingual ER site but works on its siblings, the Custom Permalinks postmeta trap is almost always the cause — diff the get_permalink() output across sites to expose it in 10 seconds

site_rules.name: elementor-image-widget-alt-source
site_rules.description: Elementor image alt has TWO render paths: rendered tag with class wp-image-N/attachment-<size> = wp_get_attachment_image = ATTACHMENT alt wins; bare tag = widget image.alt wins. Read the rendered tag to know which; when queueing blind, set BOTH.

site_rules.name: elementor-pro-posts-widget-load-more-uses-url-pagination
site_rules.description: Elementor Pro \"Posts\" widget Load More is URL-based AJAX (fetches /blog/N/), not admin-ajax POST — so any 301 on /blog/N/ silently breaks Load More just like it breaks numbered pagination

site_rules.name: erofwhiterock-cloned-from-erofirving
site_rules.description: erofwhiterock.com was built as a clone of erofirving.com (ER of Irving) and not all the content was changed. Service pages especially are at risk of duplicate content / plagiarism with the source site. Verify before rewriting and treat content originality as a live initiative, not a finished state.

site_rules.name: erofwhiterock-no-provider-bylines-yet
site_rules.description: On erofwhiterock.com specifically, do NOT propose adding provider bylines, schema Person entities, or \"Medically Reviewed by:\" lines on any page. Physicians have not yet given consent for their names to appear on the site.

site_rules.name: expert-quotes-in-blogs
site_rules.description: User wants expert quotes (name + profession) and authority external links in blog posts; only real, verifiable quotes are acceptable

site_rules.name: feedback-elementor-grid-for-icon-box-rows
site_rules.description: Icon-box rows on irvingwellnessclinic service pillars must use container_type=grid with grid_columns_grid Nfr — flex-direction=row + flex-wrap=wrap makes them stack vertically because Elementor flex children default to content-width sizing

site_rules.name: feedback-no-red-hero-band
site_rules.description: Operator (2026-08-26) rejected the composer's default full-width brand-red hero band on the ER sites as "too much for the eyes"; hero/band backgrounds should use the Secondary navy token (#11468F), red stays for CTAs, icons and accents only.

site_rules.name: feedback_location_page_doctrine
site_rules.description: 2026 doctrine for local \"location\" / service-area landing pages across the ER/local sites — when to build, when NOT to, how to differentiate, where to place

site_rules.name: gmb-utm-is-intentional
site_rules.description: /?utm_source=google&utm_medium=gmb on every site is an INTENTIONAL GMB tracking parameter — never flag as cannibalization, never recommend removing

site_rules.name: google-2026-seo-doctrine
site_rules.description: Google's documented SEO rules as of May 2026 — AI Optimization Guide, March 2026 core update site-wide signal, FAQ deprecation, back-button hijacking spam policy, deprecated schema types, named ranking systems

site_rules.name: index_client_sites
site_rules.description: Client sites and engagements index — pointers to 36 memory files; open the ones the hook names

result.notes:
# Rules ## Current evidence guidance — 2026-09-09 - Claude owns scope discovery, research and draft preparation. Use current service pages and site notes. GSC observations help prioritization but absence of queries does not mean absence of opportunities. Propose useful questions within verified services and reader needs. - Match the main reader task. Useful related explanations can belong on a service page; create a supporting article when it serves a distinct task. Do not split, merge or retire pages solely because terms overlap or clicks are low. - Compare actual sampled competitor pages and primary sources. Search position, global originality and market demand remain unknown unless independently observed. Provide a supported useful contribution such as a practical explanation, checklist or genuinely documented process. Never invent facts, research, local statistics or expert quotes. - Local audit scores and fixed citation, word or snippet quotas are not Google requirements. Support consequential claims with suitable evidence and context. Low CTR alone cannot establish why performance changed. Compare captures and investigate competing explanations. - Preserve the no-cloning rule: create new content from scratch. Preserve physician consent restrictions: no provider bylines, Person/hasCredential/sameAs markup or medically-reviewed claims without confirmed consent. Lori is not a provider at this facility. - There is one physical ER facility; neighborhood pages do not establish additional locations. Verify current capabilities, address, hours and other service claims before using them. - Keep language/category assignments explicit. Translations may faithfully serve the same reader task; they do not need invented extra facts. Verify Polylang pairing after application. - Read the actual draft/pending/applied state. Saved metadata or a prepared workflow does not prove execution or publication. Use verify_content_workflow for workflow-bound drafts. Verify rendered changes after approval. - The current user request governs the task. An older active working_state is historical context unless it matches that request. Promote new lasting constraints to Rules or Decisions; routine Sessions logs are history. - Sync only reviewed site-relevant knowledge. Do not upload unrelated sites' client files or credentials as part of this site's brain. The following retained records preserve site-specific constraints. Where an older SEO recipe conflicts with this current guidance, use current evidence; historical decisions and session notes are not renewed approval. - **Polylang pairing: ALWAYS verify after publish.** The `polylang_translation_of` arg on `draft_create_post` returns success but the actual Polylang pair often doesn't link. Symptoms: WP admin post list shows "+" icons in the EN/ES columns next to the new pair instead of the language flag. Fix: after the ES post is approved/published, run `polylang_link_translations` with the explicit `{en: X, es: Y}` pair. Idempotent on already-linked pairs. Underlying plugin bug — `draft_create_post` likely fires `pll_save_post_translations` before WP commits the draft row, so the term never writes. Plugin TODO: in `class-apply.php` create_draft_post path, move the Polylang pair call to AFTER the publish_draft pending applies (i.e. fire it in apply_publish_draft, not on insert). - **Content must add new insights and data, not just rehash.** Every post we publish has to bring something the reader cannot get from a single Google search. Two-part rule: 1. **Add new insights and data — yes.** Concrete: cite a specific authority (AAP guideline, CDC stat, NIDDK threshold, Texas DSHS volume), then frame what that data means for our catchment (White Rock Lake, Lake Highlands, East Dallas) and what action it triggers at home or in the ER. The data point + the local-action framing IS the insight. 2. **Drop the opinion layer.** We are not the first to write about appendicitis or food poisoning, so a "we believe…" / "we think the best approach is…" framing is hollow. Anchor every claim to a guideline, a peer-reviewed source, or a fact we can show is true (our own imaging turnaround, our transfer relationships, etc.). Editorial color is fine; freestanding opinion is not. **How to apply when drafting:** identify the reader task, necessary baseline explanation and supported useful contribution before writing. Inspect existing coverage. Use appropriate primary sources for consequential claims; do not invent data or operational facts. Translations may faithfully serve the same task and do not require additional facts to satisfy a quota. - **Be terse on pending-change reports.** Report actual draft, pending and applied states after checking the records. Never assume automatic approval or publication from old notes. Give the concrete result and any unresolved issue concisely. - **Local landing pages (Garland / Lake Highlands / Lakewood / etc.) are HUB pages, not satellite locations.** ER of White Rock has ONE physical facility at 10705 Northwest Highway. The neighborhood pages (e.g. `/emergency-room-garland-tx/`, `/emergency-room-lake-highlands-tx/`, `/emergency-room-lakewood-tx/`, and the ES `/es/sala-de-emergencias-cerca-de-*/` equivalents) are SEO hubs designed to pull traffic from those neighborhoods INTO the single White Rock facility. They do NOT have their own street address, phone number, or staff. Never suggest adding a per-neighborhood NAP — there is no separate location. Unique-value framing for these pages must be: drive-time from the neighborhood to 10705 Northwest Hwy, named local landmarks/schools/parks that orient the reader, the comparison vs the nearest hospital ER for that neighborhood, and neighborhood-specific scenarios (Lake Highlands trampoline fall, Lakewood evening jog at the lake, Garland border traffic patterns). NAP stays the canonical 10705 Northwest Hwy / (469) 943-2939 across all hub pages. - ## Content drafting + optimization rules (apply to every new post/page AND every existing-post optimization) 1. **Niche and demand research**: use current services, audience questions, existing coverage and available GSC observations. GSC is optional evidence; absent queries do not mean no opportunity. Never fabricate demand. 2. **Comparable-page research**: inspect actual relevant competitor pages and primary sources. Record URLs, capture dates and coverage; do not call them top-ranking without observed search evidence. Develop a supported useful contribution without copying or claiming global novelty. 3. **User-first alongside keyword/competitor**: the post serves the reader first. Keyword and competitor optimization shape what we cover and how we structure it, but the prose, tone, and depth must answer the user's real question better than any competitor — not stuffed with keywords or built for the algorithm. 4. **Useful contribution**: answer the reader task accurately and add supported practical value where useful. Do not invent facts, local statistics, research, expert quotes or service capabilities. Physician-consent restrictions still apply. An absence in sampled competitor excerpts does not establish uniqueness. **These rules apply universally**: new blog posts, new pages, optimization of existing posts, optimization of existing pages. - ## Paragraph breaks follow MEANING, not sentence counts (REVISES the older "2-3 sentence max" rule) The earlier "2-3 sentences max per paragraph" guidance was a crude band-aid for wall-of-text paste-ins from Google Docs. It is NOT the actual writing principle. From 2026-05-13 forward use the meaning-based rule below for every new post/page AND every optimization of an existing post/page: - **Break the paragraph when**: the idea shifts, the argument pivots, the path or direction of the prose changes, you want a sentence to be remembered (emphasis), or you set up a contrast that needs to land. - **Stay together when**: every sentence develops the same point and breaking would lose the thread. Forcing a break mid-argument creates choppy, robotic prose. - **Single-sentence paragraphs are GREAT** when the sentence carries weight on its own. Example: *"Real drowning is silent."* deserves its own line. *"We also have on-site CT."* does not. Use single-sentence paragraphs for punchlines, pivots, contrasts, or memorability anchors that the reader should walk away with. - **4-5 sentence paragraphs are FINE** when every sentence develops the same point and they truly need each other. A coherent argument step does not need to be artificially broken. - The standard is flow + emphasis + meaning, not sentence count. NYT, The Atlantic, and patient-facing NEJM material all follow this. So do we. This applies to every word the cc-assistant tool writes or edits on this site: new blog posts, new pages, optimization of existing posts, optimization of existing pages, and meta/title/description copy. - User constraints set 2026-05-20: (1) Lori does NOT work for erofwhiterock — never propose her name (she's at irvingwellnessclinic). (2) NO physician on this site has approved consent to be named publicly, so do NOT propose bylines, schema Person, or "Medically Reviewed by:" lines anywhere — Prioritize supported consequential claims, useful explanations and relevant internal links while preserving the consent restriction. NOT named-author. (3) erofwhiterock was built as a clone of erofirving.com; service pages especially carry unmodified Irving content. Both sites MCP-accessible — diff directly. (4) Scope approval given for adding new structural sections where pages have poor spacing/structure. Priority: rewrite for uniqueness + restructure + add information gain (CDC/NIH/Texas DSHS stats framed for White Rock catchment). - NEVER position our ER's speed by comparing against hospital EDs (even with cited stats like ED Benchmarking Alliance). Hospitals are referral partners; comparison wording erodes patient trust in hospitals AND damages referral relationships. Self-anchored door-to-provider claims only ("under 10 minutes, every visit"). ER vs urgent care vs primary care comparisons ARE allowed (decision-aid, not knock-marketing). Enforced via plugin v0.35+ `hospital_comparison_check` lint. - FREESTANDING-ER BOUNDARY (permanent): we are an independent freestanding ER. Never claim hospital affiliation, never compare against hospital EDs, never drift into urgent-care/wellness positioning, always disclose no Medicare/Medicaid billing where payment is discussed. PAGE-LANE MAP (anti-cannibalization): homepage 228 owns "er near me / emergency room dallas"; hub 3505 owns "emergency room services / conditions we treat" catalog (cards stay 1-2 line teasers linking to service pages); each /services/* page owns its condition; location pages own neighborhoods. Never write deep condition content on the hub. - DESIGN SYSTEM (enforced in build_page_from_spec v0.43.3 + audit): (1) Icons must be DISTINCT + semantic per card, FA5-named (render on FA5+FA6); never the default star. (2) Icon color = brand-navy by default, brand-RED only for danger cards (severe/911/avoid/do-not). Red != positive. (3) Buttons: first = solid primary, rest = outline secondary; never two identical solids. On dark/colored bands buttons invert (white fill + brand label / white outline) so they never blend. (4) Full-bleed bands carrying BODY text use NAVY not red (white-on-#DA1212 ~4:1 fails WCAG AA); red is for buttons/accents/danger only. (5) Eyebrow/kicker = styled

, never a heading above H1. audit_page_design now fails icon_variety + button_contrast + eyebrow-before-h1. - BUTTON + FAQ recipe (erofwhiterock, from mirror 5342): buttons radius 2, padding 18/32, border 1px, Montserrat 16/700; hover INVERTS (solid red<->white bg/red text; white-outline<->white bg/navy text). FAQ accordion: title stays h3 tag but sized 18px/600 Montserrat, title_color=text token, tab_active/icon=secondary token. cc-assistant v0.43.5 build_page_from_spec now SAMPLES these from the style mirror automatically (sample_recipe) so every built page self-matches the site — don't hardcode radius/font. - ES (Spanish/Polylang) pages: do NOT set a custom_permalink with an "es/..." path — Custom Permalinks + Polylang collide and every URL 404s (it forces /es/servicios/... which has no rewrite). Let Polylang serve ES pages natively at /es/{post_slug}/. EN pages can keep custom_permalink (services/...) since EN is the default language with no prefix. Fix when an ES page 404s: clear the custom_permalink postmeta (set empty). Hit this on ES head injury 5366 (built from 5360); cleared via #1332. Apply the same to the abdominal ES twin (use a clean slug, no custom_permalink). - BUILD CONVENTION (build_page_from_spec): a page typically has 3 CTA bands (hero, a mid-page band, final). Hero + final use the full "Call (469) 943-2939"; the MID band button must be "Call Us Now" (ES: "Llmenos Ahora") — otherwise 3 identical Call buttons trip the duplicate_card_text publish gate (hard block). Hit on TBI 5381 (fixed by varying mid button #1349). Plugin TODO (banked): make duplicate_card_text ignore repeated CTA button labels so this convention isn't needed. - DESIGN, don't template (user-flagged on TBI: 4 identical card-grid sections, 1 image not 2, blank circle-info icon). Service pages MUST vary section layouts by content type: sequential->steps (new template, numbered, no card chrome), explainer->text_image split, parallel catalog->card_grid, comparison->table, Q&A->faq, CTA->cta_band. cc-assistant v0.43.9 ENFORCES: >=2 image text_image sections + refuses 4+ card_grids without >=2 steps/text_image variety (422 monotonous_layout) + auto-normalizes FA6 icon names->FA5 so icons never blank. Author FA5 icon names (info-circle not circle-info etc.). All encoded in design-system-global skill SS I/J/K (read at session start). Operating principle: assume expert in the task and execute to standard from move one. EARLIER PAGES (head injury/abdominal/concussion/TBI EN+ES) were built pre-0.43.9 with the card-grid monotony — rebuild their layouts with steps/text_image variety when revisited. - **Expert-quote + byline standard (network-wide, adopted from eroflufkin 2026-07-16).** Every blog post: MINIMUM 2 verified expert quotes when 2 verifiable ones exist (1 acceptable otherwise). Quotes must be PREVIOUSLY PUBLISHED statements the person actually said: verify verbatim by fetching the source page, attribute exact name + credential + role at time of statement, hyperlink the source. NEVER fabricate or draft words for a real person, even gated on their sign-off (operator rejected that approach). # Rules ## Current evidence guidance — 2026-09-09 - Claude owns scope discovery, research and draft preparation. Use current service pages and site notes. GSC observations help prioritization but absence of queries does not mean absence of opportunities. Propose useful questions within verified services and reader needs. - Match the main reader task. Useful related explanations can belong on a service page; create a supporting article when it serves a distinct task. Do not split, merge or retire pages solely because terms overlap or clicks are low. - Compare actual sampled competitor pages and primary sources. Search position, global originality and market demand remain unknown unless independently observed. Provide a supported useful contribution such as a practical explanation, checklist or genuinely documented process. Never invent facts, research, local statistics or expert quotes. - Local audit scores and fixed citation, word or snippet quotas are not Google requirements. Support consequential claims with suitable evidence and context. Low CTR alone cannot establish why performance changed. Compare captures and investigate competing explanations. - Preserve the no-cloning rule: create new content from scratch. Preserve physician consent restrictions: no provider bylines, Person/hasCredential/sameAs markup or medically-reviewed claims without confirmed consent. Lori is not a provider at this facility. - There is one physical ER facility; neighborhood pages do not establish additional locations. Verify current capabilities, address, hours and other service claims before using them. - Keep language/category assignments explicit. Translations may faithfully serve the same reader task; they do not need invented extra facts. Verify Polylang pairing after application. - Read the actual draft/pending/applied state. Saved metadata or a prepared workflow does not prove execution or publication. Use verify_content_workflow for workflow-bound drafts. Verify rendered changes after approval. - The current user request governs the task. An older active working_state is historical context unless it matches that request. Promote new lasting constraints to Rules or Decisions; routine Sessions logs are history. - Sync only reviewed site-relevant knowledge. Do not upload unrelated sites' client files or credentials as part of this site's brain. The following retained records preserve site-specific constraints. Where an older SEO recipe conflicts with this current guidance, use current evidence; historical decisions and session notes are not renewed approval. - **Polylang pairing: ALWAYS verify after publish.** The `polylang_translation_of` arg on `draft_create_post` returns success but the actual Polylang pair often doesn't link. Symptoms: WP admin post list shows "+" icons in the EN/ES columns next to the new pair instead of the language flag. Fix: after the ES post is approved/published, run `polylang_link_translations` with the explicit `{en: X, es: Y}` pair. Idempotent on already-linked pairs. Underlying plugin bug — `draft_create_post` likely fires `pll_save_post_translations` before WP commits the draft row, so the term never writes. Plugin TODO: in `class-apply.php` create_draft_post path, move the Polylang pair call to AFTER the publish_draft pending applies (i.e. fire it in apply_publish_draft, not on insert). - **Content must add new insights and data, not just rehash.** Every post we publish has to bring something the reader cannot get from a single Google search. Two-part rule: 1. **Add new insights and data — yes.** Concrete: cite a specific authority (AAP guideline, CDC stat, NIDDK threshold, Texas DSHS volume), then frame what that data means for our catchment (White Rock Lake, Lake Highlands, East Dallas) and what action it triggers at home or in the ER. The data point + the local-action framing IS the insight. 2. **Drop the opinion layer.** We are not the first to write about appendicitis or food poisoning, so a "we believe…" / "we think the best approach is…" framing is hollow. Anchor every claim to a guideline, a peer-reviewed source, or a fact we can show is true (our own imaging turnaround, our transfer relationships, etc.). Editorial color is fine; freestanding opinion is not. **How to apply when drafting:** identify the reader task, necessary baseline explanation and supported useful contribution before writing. Inspect existing coverage. Use appropriate primary sources for consequential claims; do not invent data or operational facts. Translations may faithfully serve the same task and do not require additional facts to satisfy a quota. - **Be terse on pending-change reports.** Report actual draft, pending and applied states after checking the records. Never assume automatic approval or publication from old notes. Give the concrete result and any unresolved issue concisely. - **Local landing pages (Garland / Lake Highlands / Lakewood / etc.) are HUB pages, not satellite locations.** ER of White Rock has ONE physical facility at 10705 Northwest Highway. The neighborhood pages (e.g. `/emergency-room-garland-tx/`, `/emergency-room-lake-highlands-tx/`, `/emergency-room-lakewood-tx/`, and the ES `/es/sala-de-emergencias-cerca-de-*/` equivalents) are SEO hubs designed to pull traffic from those neighborhoods INTO the single White Rock facility. Whether you require life-saving cardiac panels, complex blood cultures, or rapid viral testing, our experienced emergency physicians rely on our in-house technology to deliver precise results in minutes. Experience highly capable diagnostic medicine with minimal wait times right here in East Dallas.

On-site lab testing is the core differentiator between emergency care and urgent care. Our freestanding ER vs hospital ER guide near White Rock explains how diagnostics differ between the two settings.

settings.title: Why Choose ER of White Rock for Diagnostic Testing?

settings.editor:
We do not send your critical samples across the city to a third-party facility. By processing your tests on-site, we eliminate delays and accelerate your treatment. Here is why our facility is the top choice for rapid testing:

  • COLA-Certified Laboratory: Our facility adheres to the strictest national quality control standards, ensuring your results are flawless and highly accurate.
  • Results in Minutes, Not Days: We specialize in STAT emergency testing. For most critical panels, your physician will have the data they need to treat you within one hour.
  • Affordable & Transparent Pricing: We believe in honest billing. We process most major commercial insurance plans and are committed to a strict no balance billing policy.
  • Total Privacy & Compliance: Your medical data is strictly confidential and fully HIPAA-compliant. We offer discreet processing for infectious diseases and specialized panels.

image.alt: Why Choose Our Laboratory Testing Services

settings.editor: Our state-of-the-art lab is equipped to run a massive array of critical diagnostic tests to pinpoint exactly what is happening inside your body.

When you are experiencing a medical emergency, rapid blood analysis is our first line of defense. Our on-site laboratory is equipped to run comprehensive emergency blood tests to instantly identify severe infections, organ failure, and metabolic crises.

  • Complete Blood Count (CBC): We instantly check your red and white blood cells to detect severe bacterial infections, acute blood loss, or dangerous immune responses.
  • Comprehensive Metabolic Panels: We evaluate your kidney function, liver health, and electrolyte balance to diagnose severe dehydration or diabetic emergencies.
  • Cardiac & Coagulation Panels: For patients with chest pain, we run immediate cardiac enzyme tests to detect active heart attacks and blood tests to rule out life-threatening blood clots.
  • Rapid Urinalysis: We rapidly analyze urine samples to detect painful urinary tract infections (UTIs), kidney stones, and severe kidney distress so we can administer IV antibiotics immediately.

If you suspect exposure to an infectious disease or are experiencing severe, painful symptoms, waiting days for a standard clinic appointment is incredibly stressful. We provide highly accurate, rapid, and completely confidential testing in a safe, private environment.

  • Comprehensive STD Panels: Our laboratory provides highly discreet, fast-acting diagnostic tests for Syphilis, Gonorrhea, Chlamydia, and HIV.
  • Rapid Viral Screening: We offer immediate testing for severe infectious diseases, including Hepatitis B and C, so you can understand your status fast.
  • Immediate Medical Intervention: Unlike a standalone commercial lab, our experienced emergency physicians are on-site to instantly review your results and prescribe the necessary antibiotics or antiviral medications before you leave our facility.
  • Total Patient Privacy: Your medical data and test results are strictly confidential, fully HIPAA-compliant, and processed securely right here in our White Rock facility.

settings.title: Advanced Diagnostic Capabilities in White Rock, TX

settings.editor: Our East Dallas medical team utilizes these specific laboratory tests to diagnose and treat severe medical conditions every single day:

settings.description_text_b: We offer rapid COVID-19 testing and highly accurate PCR tests to detect active infections. Whether you have a high fever or severe respiratory symptoms, we provide definitive answers fast.

Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) can be dangerous, especially for young children and older adults. We provide rapid RSV testing to detect aggressive infections early and begin immediate airway management.

background_a_image.alt: Cardiac Enzyme Testing for Heart Health

settings.description_text_b: Unexplained chest pain is always a medical emergency. We measure specific protein levels in your blood to assess heart muscle damage and definitively diagnose a cardiac event.

background_a_image.alt: Basic Metabolic Panel (BMP) for Overall Health

settings.description_text_b: A BMP provides a critical snapshot of your body's internal chemistry, including kidney function, blood sugar levels, and electrolyte balance. It is vital for diagnosing severe dehydration and diabetic crises.

background_a_image.alt: Complete Blood Count (CBC) for Infections & Immune Health

settings.description_text_b: A CBC is the foundation of emergency diagnostics. It allows our doctors to instantly detect systemic infections, severe anemia, and dangerous immune system disorders.

background_a_image.alt: Liver Function Panel for Detecting Liver Conditions

settings.description_text_b: This panel checks vital liver enzymes and proteins to assess liver toxicity and detect severe conditions such as acute hepatitis, cirrhosis, and sudden organ damage.

background_a_image.alt: Strep and Mono Testing for Sore Throats & Infections

settings.description_text_b: Severe throat pain combined with a fever requires fast identification. We provide rapid strep tests and mono tests to diagnose the exact bacterial or viral strain causing your agony.

background_a_image.alt: Urinalysis for Kidney & Urinary Tract Health

settings.description_text_b: A rapid urinalysis helps us diagnose painful urinary tract infections (UTIs), kidney stones, and complex metabolic disorders so we can administer the correct IV antibiotics.

settings.title: Who Relies on Our ER Laboratory Testing?

settings.editor:
Our COLA-certified laboratory is built for speed and precision. We provide critical diagnostic answers for patients who do not have the luxury of time.

  • Patients in a Medical Crisis: If you are experiencing sudden chest pain, severe abdominal cramping, or unexplainable weakness, our laboratory provides the immediate data our doctors need to save your life.
  • Local East Dallas Families: When a child spikes a dangerously high fever or shows signs of severe respiratory illness, parents rely on our rapid viral and bacterial testing for fast peace of mind.
  • Post-Accident Evaluations: Following a severe workplace injury or motor vehicle accident, we perform comprehensive blood panels and immediate toxicology screens to ensure safe medical interventions.

settings.title: How Our White Rock Laboratory Testing Works

settings.editor:
Medical emergencies do not operate on a schedule, and neither do we. We have streamlined our laboratory process to get you evaluated and tested immediately.

  • Step 1: Walk-In 24/7 Do not wait for an appointment. Drive directly to our modern facility anytime, day or night, and experience our standard of minimal wait times.
  • Step 2: Rapid Physician Triage If you are experiencing pain or severe symptoms, our experienced emergency doctors will evaluate you instantly to determine exactly which lab tests are required to save your life.
  • Step 3: On-Site Sample Collection Our skilled, compassionate registered nurses will draw your blood or collect necessary swabs quickly and safely in a private room.
  • Step 4: Fast, Accurate Results Your samples are walked directly to our in-house lab. Most critical test results are delivered straight to your attending physician within one hour.

settings.title: Why East Dallas Trusts Our On-Site Laboratory

settings.editor: With a reputation for excellence, our Dallas-based laboratory testing services are trusted by thousands. We blend cutting-edge technology with a patient-first approach, ensuring top-tier service and accurate results every time.

settings.description_text_b: We process your blood work and diagnostic swabs immediately on-site so you never wait days for critical medical answers.
Your lab results are not just processed; they are reviewed instantly by experienced emergency room physicians to guarantee immediate, accurate treatment.
Centrally located on Northwest Highway, we provide rapid access to high-tier medical testing with minimal wait times, saving you from the crowded hospital lobby.
From life-saving cardiac panels to rapid infectious disease screening, our freestanding emergency room has the advanced machinery to diagnose severe conditions instantly.
